items.title: Canva Is Tackling AI Design’s Most Frustrating Problem with Stefano Corazza- #784
items.summary: In this episode, Stefano Corazza, head of AI research at Canva, joins us to explore how his team is building custom models and agents around iterative design workflows. We discuss the tradeoffs between training models from scratch and adapting open weights models, and how proprietary design data supports specialization. Stefano explains how Craft separates layout planning from pixel generation and how Brush uses design tools and visual feedback to create and revise compositions. We examine the challenges of evaluating design quality beyond a single generation, including the use of vision language models as judges alongside human evaluation. We also discuss lessons from simplifying agent harnesses, why faster inference enables more iterations, and how model ownership creates opportunities to optimize serving costs. Finally, we explore how APIs and MCP are expanding access to these capabilities and what changes when software companies build tools for agents as well as people. 🗒️ Full show notes: ⁠⁠ https://twimlai.com/go/784 .

items.title: What Leaders Should Scope Before Investing in an AI Model - with Melissa Ramey of Salesforce
items.summary: Choosing an AI model without defining the task can leave organizations paying for capabilities they do not need or relying on tools that cannot handle the work. In this episode, Melissa Ramey, Director, AI Transformation – Data Insights and User Experience at Salesforce, joins Emerj's Yolandi de Weerdt to examine how leaders can evaluate models against the work their teams need done. She discusses testing models on everyday tasks, involving employees in workflow assessment, and revisiting performance as requirements change.
